title: Transformer-Based Sarcasm Detection in News Headlines Using BERT
abstract: Sarcasm detection is a challenging problem in sentiment analysis because sarcastic expressions often convey meanings that differ from their literal wording. Detecting sarcasm is important for improving the reliability of opinion mining, social media analysis, and customer feedback interpretation. This study proposes a transformer-based sarcasm detection system using the News Headlines Sarcasm Dataset. A baseline model using TF-IDF features with Logistic Regression is first implemented to establish a reference performance, achieving an accuracy of 82.84%. Subsequently, a fine-tuned BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) model is applied to capture contextual relationships and semantic dependencies within headlines. The dataset is preprocessed and divided into training, validation, and testing sets to ensure reliable evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed BERT-based model achieves an accuracy of 93.85%, significantly outperforming the baseline model. The results highlight the effectiveness of transformer-based contextual language models for identifying subtle linguistic patterns in sarcastic text.

title: Evaluating Explanation Faithfulness in Lightweight Image Classifiers Using Grad-CAM and Counterfactual Patches
abstract: Objectives: This study evaluates whether visual explanations from lightweight image classifiers are faithful to model behaviour, rather than only visually plausible. The paper compares Grad-CAM heat maps with minimal counterfactual patch edits for pet-breed image classification. Methods: MobileNetV2 and a Small CNN were trained on the Oxford–IIIT Pet data-set using the official test split. Classification was assessed using accuracy, macro-F1 and per-class performance. Explanation quality was evaluated on a balanced sample of 370 test images using deletion confidence drop, random-mask comparison, stability under brightness perturbation, object-focus overlap with tri-map masks, counterfactual flip success, edited pixel fraction, SSIM and confidence-stratified analysis. Results: MobileNetV2 achieved strong test performance, with accuracy of 0.8787 and macro-F1 of 0.8769, while the Small CNN performed weakly, with accuracy of 0.1646 and macro-F1 of 0.1529. MobileNetV2 Grad-CAM maps were highly object-focused and stable, with mean object focus of 0.8982 and stability IoU of 0.9627. However, deletion testing produced a negative deletion advantage of -0.0648, indicating that Grad-CAM regions did not reduce confidence more than random regions on average. Counterfactual patches achieved a MobileNetV2 flip success rate of 0.4486, mean SSIM of 0.9587 and object focus of 0.9231. Conclusion: Grad-CAM is useful for localisation and inspection, but it should not be treated as standalone evidence of faithfulness. Counterfactual patches provide stronger behavioural sensitivity evidence, although they are computationally expensive and can appear artificial.

title: Improved Knowledge-Based Reinforcement Learning in DBN Model with Significant Biomarker for Cervical Cancer Detection and Classification
abstract: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer affecting women worldwide and results from persistent infections of high-risk HPVs by virtue of their oncogenic effects of the E6 and E7 proteins. In this paper, a new technique for diagnosing cervical cancer based on biomarkers and genes such as KRT17 and CRISP2, and a new IKRL-DBN framework that improves upon conventional models by mitigating the vanishing gradient problem through weighted layer-wise information reinforcement, are proposed. The model improves upon existing models by combining weighted layer-wise information reinforcement with gradient descent, making it more robust and efficient than other frameworks. In addition to the statistical analysis, it has been shown that IKRL-DBN achieved a remarkably high accuracy rate of 95.0% relative to other baseline models such as DBN, CNN, SVM, and Random Forest. Notably, the IKRL-DBN achieved a relatively high recall score, 10.5% higher than that of SVM, which is highly significant for reducing false negatives. From the ablation tests, it was confirmed that domain-specific features play an essential role in prediction since removing them caused the accuracy to decrease by 5.0%. The test also verified that the weighted reinforcement component plays an important role in ensuring the stability and consistency of the learning of the model. Moreover, the statistics for dimensional reduction using PCA and t-SNE showed significant improvements in class separability when using biomarkers and problem-specific weights and relations, with 76.4% to 91.7% improvements. In future research, the model's effectiveness should be verified using more extensive datasets and incorporating other types of data and methodologies.

title: Multi-Theory Automated Scientific Discovery: Extracting Galois Adjunctions and Lattice Meets/Joins from Universal Hypergraph Geometries
abstract: Opzione 1: Focus sulla Teoria Matematica Generale Italiano Titolo: Scoperta Scientifica Automatizzata Multi-Teoria: Estrazione di Aggiunzioni di Galois e Reticoli di Meet/Join da Geometrie di Ipergrafi Universali Descrizione (Abstract): Questo lavoro presenta un framework computazionale avanzato per la scoperta scientifica automatizzata (in silico) basato sull'analisi topologica e algebrica di ipergrafi universali strutturati. Utilizzando il motore di inferenza Multi-Theory Abduction Engine sul dataset ipergrafo_Universale_di_Luigi_Usai17.ndjsonld, dimostriamo come sia possibile estrarre relazioni trans-dominio non esplicite integrando tre pilastri della matematica formale: la teoria delle categorie (composizione di morfismi su cammini sequenziali di lunghezza da 2 a 15), la teoria degli ordini (connessioni e aggiunzioni di Galois) e la teoria dei reticoli (calcolo algebrico dei supremi e infimi relativi, ovvero Join e Meet). Il sistema ha generato e classificato con successo un set di 45.720 abduzioni univoche, ripartite secondo criteri di dominazione epistemica in abduzioni note (gruppo di controllo per la calibrazione del modello) e abduzioni speculative/nuove. La robustezza sintattica e l'assoluta univocità degli identificatori strutturati (basati su hashing crittografico del cammino topologico) validano l'architettura come un motore deterministico per l'estrazione di leggi scientifiche sintetiche, ridefinendo il paradigma della ricerca trans-disciplinare quantitativa. English Title: Multi-Theory Automated Scientific Discovery: Extracting Galois Adjunctions and Lattice Meets/Joins from Universal Hypergraph Geometries Description (Abstract): This paper presents an advanced computational framework for in silico automated scientific discovery based on the topological and algebraic analysis of structured universal hypergraphs. Utilizing a customized Multi-Theory Abduction Engine on the ipergrafo_Universale_di_Luigi_Usai17.ndjsonld dataset, we demonstrate the extraction of non-explicit cross-domain relationships by integrating three pillars of formal mathematics: category theory (composition of path morphisms with lengths ranging from 2 to 15), order theory (Galois connections and adjunctions), and lattice theory (algebraic computation of relative suprema and infima, namely Join and Meet). The architecture successfully generated and classified a dataset of 45,720 unique abductions, partitioned via epistemic dominance heuristics into known abductions (acting as a control group for model calibration) and speculative/novel abductions. The syntactic robustness and absolute uniqueness of the structured identifiers—ensured via cryptographic hashing of the topological paths—validate the architecture as a deterministic engine for synthetic scientific law extraction, reshaping the paradigm of quantitative cross-disciplinary research. Opzione 2: Focus sul Controllo dei Flussi Biochimici Italiano Titolo: Coomologia di Hodge-de Rham Discreta come Protocollo di Controllo per la Stabilizzazione dei Flussi Biochimici in Reti Biologiche Complesse Descrizione (Abstract): Le reti biochimiche sono sistemi aperti, fuori dall'equilibrio termodinamico, caratterizzati da dinamiche non lineari, multi-stabilità e transizioni caotiche. Questo preprint definisce un framework di controllo matematico formale basato sulla geometria differenziale discreta (Discrete Exterior Calculus) e sulla coomologia di de Rham-Bott-Chern. Modellando i pathway metabolici come complessi simpliciali e i flussi biochimici come forme differenziali discrete, si dimostra che l'omeostasi e la stabilità dinamica possono essere governate proiettando ortogonalmente gli stati vettoriali sul nucleo del Laplaciano di Hodge discreto (spazio delle forme armoniche). Viene presentata l'applicazione di questo protocollo di controllo coomologico per la stabilizzazione dei flussi oscillatori della glicolisi/TCA, dei rapporti autofagici LC3-I/II e degli ensemble conformazionali della proteina alfa-sinucleina. Il modello introduce criteri stringenti di falsificabilità basati sull'isomorfismo bidirezionale tra le dimensioni dei campi armonici discreti e le varietà continue corrispondenti. English Title: Discrete Hodge-de Rham Cohomology as a Governing Control Protocol for Biochemical Flux Stabilization in Complex Biological Networks Description (Abstract): Biochemical networks are open, non-equilibrium systems exhibiting complex non-linear oscillations, multi-stability, and chaotic transitions. This paper establishes a formal mathematical control framework rooted in Discrete Exterior Calculus and de Rham-Bott-Chern cohomology. By modeling metabolic pathways as simplicial complexes where biochemical flux vectors are represented as discrete differential forms, we prove that homeostatic stability can be governed by orthogonally projecting active states onto the kernel of the discrete Hodge Laplacian operator (harmonic space). We demonstrate the applicability of this cohomological control protocol to stabilize Glycolysis/TCA oscillatory fluxes, autophagy LC3-I/II degradation ratios, and alpha-synuclein conformational ensembles. The model introduces strict falsifiability criteria based on the bijective dimension match between discrete harmonic fields and their corresponding smooth manifold approximations. ITALIANO Titolo Scoperta Scientifica Automatizzata Multi-Teoria: Estrazione di Aggiunzioni di Galois e Reticoli di Meet/Join da Geometrie di Ipergrafi Universali con Estensione ad Architetture D-Wave Descrizione / Abstract Questo lavoro presenta un framework computazionale avanzato per la scoperta scientifica automatizzata (in silico) basato sull'analisi topologica e algebrica di ipergrafi universali strutturati. Utilizzando il motore di inferenza Multi-Theory Abduction Engine sul dataset ipergrafo_Universale_di_Luigi_Usai17.ndjsonld, dimostriamo come sia possibile estrarre relazioni trans-dominio non esplicite integrando tre pilastri della matematica formale: la teoria delle categorie (composizione di morfismi su cammini sequenziali di lunghezza da 2 a 15), la teoria degli ordini (connessioni e aggiunzioni di Galois) e la teoria dei reticoli (calcolo algebrico dei supremi e infimi relativi, ovvero Join e Meet). Il sistema ha generato e classificato con successo un set di 45.720 abduzioni univoche, ripartite secondo criteri di dominazione epistemica in abduzioni note (gruppo di controllo per la calibrazione del modello) e abduzioni speculative/nuove. La robustezza sintattica e l'assoluta univocità degli identificatori strutturati (basati su hashing crittografico del cammino topologico) validano l'architettura come un motore deterministico per l'estrazione di leggi scientifiche sintetiche. A completamento del framework, viene formalizzata l'estensione dell'architettura verso la Biologia e la Chimica Quantistica Computazionale. Viene delineata la mappatura dell'ipergrafo universale in una funzione di costo QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) e nel modello di Ising per vetri di spin, consentendo la scalabilità dei cammini logici oltre i vincoli classici di tipo NP-hard. Attraverso l'integrazione dell'operatore Laplaciano di Hodge discreto nella topologia fisica dei qubit di un processore ad annealing quantistico D-Wave (architetture Zephyr o Pegasus), si dimostra come il sistema possa risolvere per via fisica, tramite il raggiungimento del Ground State termodinamico, i vettori di flusso stazionari e omeostatici (forme armoniche) di reti biochimiche complesse, assegnando una distribuzione di Boltzmann e un punteggio di confidenza probabilistico-quantistico reale alle scoperte generate in silico. title: Surveillance Dynamique Interne du Flux Résiduel : Détection et Correction de la Dérive Algorithmique dans les Grands Modèles de Langage
abstract: Résumé Les grands modèles de langage (LLM) souffrent d’hallucinations non pas comme de simples erreurs statistiques, mais comme des défaillances dynamiques de la géométrie représentationnelle interne. Cet article propose un nouveau cadre de surveillance dynamique interne du flux résiduel. Nous formalisons la transition du raisonnement ancré vers la dérive algorithmique à travers la dégradation de la similarité cosinus inter-couches. En définissant un Score de Dérive D(t) en temps réel basé sur la divergence géométrique par fenêtre glissante, nous établissons un critère de détection pré-lexicale qui identifie la défaillance logique avant qu’elle ne se manifeste dans la sortie textuelle. De plus, nous introduisons un mécanisme d’intervention automatique par projection dans le sous-espace de véracité pour corriger la trajectoire du flux résiduel en temps réel. Des résultats empiriques simulés dé- montrent que ce système de surveillance réduit les taux d’hallucination de 74%, transformant la boîte noire opaque en un système dynamique contrôlable.

title: Fine-tuning for Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer on XTREME
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tasks a Research goal: Can fine-tuning a model on a combination of English and non-English intermediate tasks further improve zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME, and how does this compare to English-only intermediate-task training? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.0/10.

title: Climate data generation employing meteonorm model over selected stations in Iraq
abstract: Climate is the average weather conditions for a region for a long time, it is also assuming as a relation between weather phenomena and environment whether its natural or human made. The aim of this work is to generate climatological normal for selected cities in Iraq using the software package meteonorm weather and climate generator. The results showed that the temperature during summer in Mosul and Baghdad may reach more than (42oC) while in Rutba and Basra temperature may reach above (38oC) and (48oC) respectively, while the temperature during winter can reach values close to freezing level in Mosul, Baghdad and Rutba while Basra temperature dose not reach such level. The difference in the highest value of diffuse and global radiation (low diffuse - high global) in Rutba city is attributed to the fact that this city is rural which means that it has relatively low pollution particles. The highest maximum sunshine occurs in the Mosul because it is located relatively on high latitude while highest minimum sunshine occurs in the Basra because of low cloud cover during the year.

title: Intelligent System for Diagnosing Infectious Diseases in Children Using the Certainty Factor and Naive Bayes Methods Based on Android
abstract: Infectious diseases in children remain a serious health problem due to their high vulnerability resulting from an immune system that is not yet fully developed. Limited access to medical personnel and delays in early detection often result in ineffective treatment. Therefore, this study aims to design and implement an Android-based intelligent system application capable of detecting infectious diseases in children early on by utilizing the Certainty Factor and Naïve Bayes methods. This system is designed as an expert system that mimics the way pediatricians analyze symptoms and determine preliminary diagnoses. The research methods used include collecting disease and symptom data based on the knowledge of pediatric health experts, data analysis, rule base formation, and the design and implementation of an Android-based system. The Certainty Factor method is used to handle the uncertainty of the level of confidence in the symptoms selected by the user, while the Naïve Bayes method is used to calculate the probability of disease based on historical data. The combination of these two methods aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of diagnostic results. The results of the study show that the developed expert system application is capable of providing initial diagnostic information on infectious diseases in children quickly and easily accessible to parents and health workers. This system is expected to be an effective early detection tool, support initial medical decision-making, and contribute to the development of artificial intelligence-based health technology in Indonesia.

title: TRE: Training-Free Hallucination Detection for Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Diffusion large language models (D-LLMs) have recently gained increasing attention, yet their reliability is significantly hindered by the hallucination problem. Existing hallucination detection approaches for D-LLMs mainly follow a training-based paradigm, relying on data-driven training to optimize the detector. Such reliance not only limits their generalizability across domains models but also incurs additional training cost and deployment overhead. To address these limitations, we propose TRE, a training-free hallucination detection metric for D-LLMs. TRE is a parameter-free and single-run metric that estimates hallucination risk directly from the entropy signals of a single generation, without requiring any detector training or repeated sampling. TRE extracts entropy signals within the D-LLM decoding process along both the spatial and temporal dimensions. From a token-level spatial perspective, we focus on revealing tokens as the most informative carriers of uncertainty, capturing where uncertainty is actively committed. From a diffusion step-level temporal perspective, we empirically identify the dominance of late-step entropy and hence aggregate these signals with a simple linear weighting scheme to obtain TRE. Extensive experiments on multiple D-LLMs and QA datasets demonstrate that TRE achieves competitive performance, while enjoying strong generalizability, efficiency, and robustness.

title: Structural-budgeted QUBO learning of Bayesian networks with spectral and credibility diagnostics
abstract: Traditional Bayesian network structure learning requires explicit trade-offs among structural complexity, statistical fit, and decision reliability. This study proposes BAPS (Budgeted Acyclicity with Phase-transition Spectral diagnostics), a framework that reformulates structure learning as a budget-controlled optimization problem in which a global edge budget limits the number of selected candidate edges and thereby regulates model capacity. A relaxed QUBO formulation with post-hoc DAG projection explores likelihood-improving structures while recovering feasible directed acyclic graphs; in benchmark experiments, the repair process reduces SHD by 20.6%, 14.9%, and 8.3% on Asia, Insurance, and Barley, indicating improved structural agreement while enforcing feasibility. Spectral diagnostics based on algebraic connectivity serve as descriptive structural indicators for flagging budget regions where repair burden may escalate. A dual-layer credibility framework quantifies uncertainty from parameter and observational sources; credibility interval width contracts by 69-73% under increasing Dirichlet concentration and remains empirically stable in sparse-data conditions where resampling-based methods become unstable due to zero-frequency effects. Across benchmark networks, BAPS achieves the highest BIC gain while maintaining broadly comparable held-out predictive performance relative to established baselines. Overall, BAPS provides a unified framework integrating edge-budget capacity control, structural diagnostics, feasibility repair, and credibility assessment for Bayesian network learning in complex diagnostic environments.

title: Invisible poison attacks and holistic defence strategy for pyramid vision transformers in medical imaging
abstract: Machine learning models, especially vision transformers in the domain of medical images, are highly prone to data poisoning attacks, in which a small proportion of adversarial samples is injected into the model's training dataset to manipulate its behavior. Existing data poisoning techniques have their limitations in terms of the presence of noticeable artifacts in the injected samples or their vulnerability to preprocessing transformations. Similarly, most defence techniques have their limitations in terms of robustness to different types of poisoning attacks. To overcome these challenges, this research presents a structurally embedded invisible poisoning attack technique and a Holistic Defence Strategy (HDS) for the Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) model. In this research, the proposed invisible poisoning attack technique takes advantage of the structural characteristics of images, specifically the edges of images, as invisible carriers of trigger information. The proposed attack technique develops a Deep Multi-Scale U-Net Injection Network (DMS-UNet-IN) to embed the trigger information in images in an invisible manner. The proposed attack technique differs significantly from traditional trigger-based techniques in terms of the alignment of perturbations with structural manifolds. The Holistic Defence Strategy (HDS) develops a discriminative detection boundary in the feature space using a mimic model with an attention-aware generative adversarial network. The proposed invisible poisoning attack technique was evaluated using Radiology, Ophthalmology, and Pathology datasets. The experimental evaluation of the proposed invisible poisoning attack technique showed its superiority in terms of invisibility, with a PSNR value of 43.46 dB and SSIM value of 0.9925, over the state-of-the-art techniques such as DeepPoison (40.91 dB) and SPM (38.16 dB). The proposed Holistic Defence Strategy was evaluated using static poisoning rates ranging from 5 to 30%. evidence.title: Invisible poison attacks and holistic defence strategy for pyramid vision transformers in medical imaging
evidence.abstract: Machine learning models, especially vision transformers in the domain of medical images, are highly prone to data poisoning attacks, in which a small proportion of adversarial samples is injected into the model's training dataset to manipulate its behavior. Existing data poisoning techniques have their limitations in terms of the presence of noticeable artifacts in the injected samples or their vulnerability to preprocessing transformations. Similarly, most defence techniques have their limitations in terms of robustness to different types of poisoning attacks. In this research, the proposed invisible poisoning attack technique takes advantage of the structural characteristics of images, specifically the edges of images, as invisible carriers of trigger information. The proposed attack technique develops a Deep Multi-Scale U-Net Injection Network (DMS-UNet-IN) to embed the trigger information in images in an invisible manner. The proposed attack technique differs significantly from traditional trigger-based techniques in terms of the alignment of perturbations with structural manifolds. The Holistic Defence Strategy (HDS) develops a discriminative detection boundary in the feature space using a mimic model with an attention-aware generative adversarial network. The proposed invisible poisoning attack technique was evaluated using Radiology, Ophthalmology, and Pathology datasets. The experimental evaluation of the proposed invisible poisoning attack technique showed its superiority in terms of invisibility, with a PSNR value of 43.46 dB and SSIM value of 0.9925, over the state-of-the-art techniques such as DeepPoison (40.91 dB) and SPM (38.16 dB). title: Experience replay in reinforcement learning: A systematic review
abstract: Background : Experience Replay (ER) has become a cornerstone of modern reinforcement learning (RL), enabling improved sample efficiency and training stability by reusing past experiences. Since its introduction, a diverse set of ER methods has emerged, including prioritized, hindsight, reservoir-based, episodic, and compressed replay schemes. While several narrative surveys exist, a systematic, transparent, and reproducible synthesis of this literature is still lacking. Objective : This article provides a comprehensive systematic literature review (SLR) and taxonomy of ER methods in RL. We aim to (i) categorize existing approaches across key methodological dimensions, (ii) quantify publication trends and application domains, and (iii) identify research gaps and reproducibility issues. Methods : We followed PRISMA guidelines to conduct a structured search across major scientific databases (Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and Springer). An initial pool of 3600 records was identified, from which 250 studies were assessed in full text after screening. Following quality assessment and snowballing, a final corpus of 200 studies was included in the systematic synthesis. Results : Our systematic analysis identifies clear methodological trends and clusters in experience replay research. Prioritized replay is the most widely adopted advanced sampling strategy, while hindsight replay predominates in goal-conditioned and sparse-reward tasks. The field also shows growing diversification toward episodic, memory-efficient, and multi-agent replay designs. However, reproducibility remains a concern, with only a minority of studies providing accessible code or complete experimental documentation. Conclusions : This review provides the first systematic, taxonomy-driven synthesis of ER methods in RL, highlighting both dominant trends and under-explored areas such as uncertainty-aware sampling and scalable memory architectures. All extracted datasets, tables, and screening information are released as open supplementary material to support future research.

title: The effects and financial impacts of wildfire smoke on solar photovoltaic power production in Alberta, Canada
abstract: As reliance on solar photovoltaic (PV) generation grows, particularly in Alberta, accounting for the impact of wildfire smoke on solar energy production is crucial. This is particularly relevant in regions with high PV generation potential, such as Alberta, as they are often more vulnerable to frequent and intense wildfires. This study quantifies PV energy losses and financial impacts due to wildfire smoke in Alberta, using fine particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5) as a proxy for smoke pollution. Historical weather and PM2.5 data, along with simulated PV production from actual completed, proposed, and under-construction projects, are used to train and test the model. The simulated data is validated against real production data. The six-year study (2018–2023) covers major wildfire years and employs machine learning techniques, particularly random forest regression, to isolate the effects of PM2.5 on solar production. Financial losses are estimated in Canadian dollars, adjusted for inflation to December 2023.Results show a PV production decline of up to 6.3% at a single solar site over six years, with an overall average reduction of 3.91% under severe conditions. The cumulative impact led to a 0.19% average generation loss, equating to over $4.5 million in financial losses. Higher smoke levels consistently correlate with greater solar energy losses, aligning with findings from other regions. The results of this study enhance our understanding of climate change impacts on solar energy, highlighting wildfire smoke as a relevant factor. As PV adoption expands, these findings offer valuable insights for decision-makers and operational planners, emphasizing the need for strategies to mitigate smoke-related disruptions and ensure energy reliability.

title: One Student, Many Teachers: Multi-Task On-Policy Distillation via Soft-Prompt Privileged Context
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) teaches large language models new skills through a teacher that shares the student's backbone and supervises its own rollouts. Existing teachers either inject privileged context at the input -- inducing post-hoc rationalization -- or fine-tune weights, accumulating drift and forgetting across tasks. We propose \method, whose teacher differs from the student only by a learnable soft prompt: trained on $(x, y_\text{gold})$ pairs with the backbone frozen, the prompt yields a task-specific teacher that preserves the student's exact representational geometry. \method\ extends naturally to multi-task settings by routing each example in a merged corpus to its corresponding soft-prompt teacher, allowing a single student to absorb knowledge from $K$ teachers in parallel; at inference, all prompts are discarded. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Phi-4-mini-instruct across four tasks (Science, Tool Use, Biology, Math), the single-task variant (OPD with a PT teacher) matches or exceeds full fine-tuning while training orders of magnitude fewer parameters, and the multi-task variant achieves the best overall average ($56.2$ on Qwen3-1.7B-Base) while preserving general-capability benchmarks -- in contrast to sequential SFT, which degrades both.

title: Structural Pattern Mining in Inka Khipus: Unsupervised Clustering, Provenance Classification, and a Computational Validation of the Santa Valley Match
abstract: Khipus -- knotted cord devices -- were the primary recording medium of the Inka Empire (c. 1400-1532 CE), yet their system remains undeciphered. We present a reproducible machine-learning pipeline applied to the Open Khipu Repository (OKR), a public database of 619 khipus comprising 54,403 cords and 110,677 knots. We engineer 27 structural features per khipu and apply (i) unsupervised clustering via UMAP and HDBSCAN, recovering three structurally distinct groups (silhouette = 0.769); (ii) supervised provenance classification via gradient boosting, reaching F1 = 0.86 for the Inka Late Horizon imperial style; and (iii) SHAP-based interpretability, which identifies cord twist direction as the dominant structural discriminator of imperial khipus. We further report two findings of methodological interest. First, one cluster is dominated not by a geographic region but by nineteenth-century European museum collections, indicating that colonial acquisition and recording practices are structurally encoded in the corpus. Second, we provide an independent computational verification of the recto/verso (moiety) structure of the six Santa Valley khipus reported by Medrano and Urton (2018), reproducing both the aggregate attachment ratio and the identification of the single mixed specimen--using only the public OKR database, without physical access to the objects. We additionally report a negative result: knot-type sequence order, encoded as n-grams, adds no provenance signal beyond aggregate features. All code and data are openly available.

title: Forensic Linguistics on Gender-Based Abuse and Harassment in Instagram Comments on Public Figures
abstract: This study examines gender-based abuse and harassment directed at public figures in Instagram comment sections from a forensic linguistic perspective. Social media has expanded opportunities for direct public interaction, but it has also enabled verbal violence, hate speech, defamatory expressions, and gendered attacks to circulate rapidly. The study aims to identify the linguistic forms, meanings, and structural patterns of abusive comments and to explain their potential relevance to the analysis of language-related offences. A descriptive qualitative design was employed using Instagram comments and supporting online media reports as data sources. The comments were analyzed through Hallidayan transitivity, with attention to process types, participants, attributes, and circumstances. The findings show that abusive comments are predominantly constructed through attributive and identifying relational processes that assign degrading labels to an explicit or implied target. Recurring patterns include dehumanization through animal comparisons, body-shaming, sexualized and moral attacks, and insults based on gender identity or sexual orientation. Ellipsis of the copular process, accumulation of vulgar labels, capitalization, repeated letters, and exclamation marks intensify the aggression. Mental, verbal, and material processes also appear, particularly in expressions of anger, mockery, intimidation, and threat. These findings demonstrate that online abusive language is not linguistically neutral; rather, its grammatical organization constructs unequal power relations and normalizes verbal violence. Transitivity analysis therefore offers a systematic basis for documenting how insulting meanings are encoded and for supporting context-sensitive forensic interpretation.

title: Development of an artificial intelligence assistant for air traffic control based on speech recognition and machine learning
abstract: Air Traffic Control (ATC) is a safety-critical domain where human operators manage aircraft flow through Very High Frequency (VHF) voice communications. A significant portion of these communications consists of routine, predictable interactions (such as initial contacts) that contribute to controller cognitive workload without requiring complex decision-making. This project aims to design, develop, and evaluate a low-latency automated ATCo assistant capable of handling the specific initial contact subset of communications. To meet civil aviation safety requirements, a deterministic modular architecture is proposed, integrating Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models with lightweight Machine Learning (ML) classifiers and rule-based extraction algorithms. Ten ASR architectures were evaluated, with a fine-tuned Whisper Large model achieving 92% accuracy on real ATC audio. Three Natural Language Understanding (NLU) approaches were compared; the selected modular architecture, designed specifically for this project, achieved 100% accuracy on speaker and intent classification and 84.6% callsign extraction accuracy, with a mean processing time of 4.6 milliseconds per sequence. A functional Client-Server prototype was developed to validate the complete system in a simulated operational environment, featuring a graphical interface with Text-to-Speech (TTS) response capabilities. Results confirm that deterministic, non-generative architectures can reliably automate initial ATC contacts while maintaining the safety and latency standards required by civil aviation. The remaining challenge is infrastructural: achieving full real-time operation requires GPU-accelerated hardware deployment beyond the scope of this project.

title: System Public Graph
abstract: The System Graph is a domain-agnostic, multi-scale graph with a scientifically-established finding as its atomic unit. Updated daily, using AI, and with a patented approach, the System Graph extracts, grounds, and links findings from verified sources like peer-reviewed studies and expert-curated databases. This generates millions of rich, quantitative relationships that cut across sources and fields from health, biology, climate, economics and beyond. It is a constantly growing, living representation of scientific knowledge. The System Public Graph is an annual static snapshot of a subset of the System Graph. Its contents are derived only from open, publicly available sources. The System Public Graph is made freely available for non-commercial use. It is designed to support researchers and developers across multiple disciplines, who need structured, machine-readable representations of scientific knowledge and relationships for analysis, modeling, and application development. The System Public Graph will soon be made available in other formats with more frequent updates: check System.com for updates. Documentation for the dataset: 1:Overview 2: Quick-Start Guide 3: Methods 4: Variable Grounding Logic 5: Data Provenance 6: Limitations and Known Biases 7: Data Dictionary This dataset is released under a CC-BY-NC 4.0 license. It is intended for non-commercial research and educational use.

title: A cache-coherent attestation controller for runtime memory integrity verification
abstract: Runtime memory attestation allows a verifier to confirm that a memory region contains expected code or data. Existing approaches typically read memory contents directly from DRAM, overlooking a fundamental property of cache-coherent architectures: a cache line in the Modified state represents the sole valid copy, rendering the corresponding DRAM location stale. This semantic gap implies that DRAM-based monitors cannot observe modifications residing exclusively in cache. In this thesis, I argue that participation in the cache coherence protocol is a correctness requirement for runtime memory attestation, and I present the Cache-Coherent Attestation Controller (CAC), a hardware architecture that closes this gap via a freeze-and-recall protocol. The design provides dual measurement paths: a non-coherent path for direct DRAM access to uncached regions, and a coherent path that freezes a three-level cache hierarchy, drains pending transactions, and recalls dirty lines into a snapshot buffer prior to hashing. The cache subsystem implements MESIF coherence across three PicoRV32 RISC-V cores with 16 KB private L1 caches, a 32 KB shared L2 cache, and a 64 KB shared L3 cache. Integrity is verified using SHA3-512 digests organized into SipHash-2-4 based attestation chains, while an AXI4 firewall and an intrusion prevention controller provide access control and automated threat response. The architecture is realized in synthesizable SystemVerilog and demonstrated on a Xilinx ZCU102 featuring a Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC. Directed tests validate the thesis claim: when a memory region contains Modified cache lines, non-coherent measurement yields a digest of stale DRAM contents, while coherent measurement yields a digest reflecting the true cached state. These results substantiate that coherence-aware attestation is necessary for sound integrity verification in systems employing write-back caches.

title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Computational Framework for Evaluating Arabic Literary Text Generation Using ChatGPT
abstract: Existing AI models, like those based on LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT), have successfully demonstrated text generation in Arabic; nonetheless, the evaluation of Arabic generation remains difficult because of the rich morphological system and tight stylistic constraints in Arabic literary texts. Standard n-gram and surface-similarity metrics can no longer handle multi-level properties such as Hierarchical stylistic consistency, Semantic drift, and Global narrative cohesion. This paper presents an Artificial Intelligence-Driven Computational Framework for Evaluating Arabic Literary Text Generation (AICF-ALTG), comprising stylistic (Stylometry), semantic, and discourse-level models, including Hierarchical Stylometric Entropy Modeling, Semantic Drift Trajectory Analysis, Context-Aware Narrative Coherence Index, and Human-AI Literary Alignment Estimation, to estimate the multi-level quality of an AI-generated Arabic text. Experimental results on the Arabic Poem Comprehensive Dataset (consisting of 1.83 million lines of Arabic poems) indicate that the AICF-ALTG outperforms baseline NLP evaluation approaches with respect to stylistic and semantic criteria by 31.4% and 15.2%, respectively, on averaged performance metrics on 6 different subtasks. Specifically, the Human-AI Literary Alignment Score (HALAS) and Discourse-Level Semantic Preservation Ratio (DSPR) achieve 91.4% and 93.2%, reduce coherence variance by 27.6%, embedding divergence decreases by 21.8%, and statistical tests confirm this significance at p < 0.001 across all tasks, offering reference-free, hierarchical, explainable, and flexible alternatives to existing metrics for assessing AI-generated Arabic literary texts and for computational creativity.
